scenario.title: What counts as delivered
situations: Existing project with externally owned hosting
Work can ship by merge alone
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
scenario.review: Older research may describe heavier onboarding. Apply minimum activation and optional-adoption boundaries first.
questions: Decide how the future nudge treats intentionally deferred delivery without nagging or falsely reporting readiness.

lessons.title: Choose a delivery meaning
lessons.when: Execution-profile confirmation today; when delivery matters in the planned journey
lessons.need: Persistent delivery, explicit merge-only and no default are three different answers. Host ownership is a separate fact. Read existing declarations before asking.
lessons.surface: Onboard profile lines 44–56; hosting posture and default precedence in projects-and-flows.
lessons.gap: JOURNEYS row 12 should branch on the recorded answer; absence of environments is not automatically a setup defect. Progressive timing is planned, not current.

lessons.title: Merge-only still has gates
lessons.when: User deliberately chooses delivery at merge
lessons.need: Select an active registered flow with no target tier/environment. Complete the pinned review and workflow gates without creating a deployment run.
lessons.gap: Keep a short merge-only explanation reachable from the release nudge; do not treat a missing flow as equivalent.

lessons.title: No default postpones the choice
lessons.when: User chooses no default or reconfigures an existing project
lessons.need: Read per-workflow overrides and project fallback. Omitted item flow does not waive delivery; a later planning/release gate may require a choice.
lessons.surface: Onboard no-default recipe lines 166–180; default rules lines 45–64.
lessons.gap: Verified recipe gap: no-default clears only the project fallback even though workflow defaults override it. Proposed correction must verify both layers before claiming no default.
